A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same i-LN research despite retitling and extensive reformatting. All pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original restoration experiments, normalization ablations, training-dynamics analyses and reduced-precision inference results in Tables 1–6 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: V2 retains original restoration and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and reports additional entropy and convergence diagnostics.

M1.justification: Both versions use normalization across spatial and channel dimensions followed by input-dependent rescaling of attention and feed-forward outputs. V2's generic residual-update equation restates v1's separate attention and feed-forward equations without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Training remains on DF2K and Rain13K, with the same super-resolution, denoising, deraining and JPEG-removal benchmarks. Resolution scales, noise levels, JPEG quality factors and reduced-precision scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The same restoration backbones and normalization comparators remain evaluated, including LayerScale, RMSNorm, ReZero, no normalization, InstanceNorm and BatchNorm. Eval-mode BatchNorm remains in the failure analysis despite losing its tabulated scores.

E3.justification: Entropy inspection expands from the last block in v1 Section 3.1 to multiple layers in v2 Figure 1, and the rescaling evaluation gains entropy measurements. Reported core training settings remain unchanged. Omitted color-space and border-cropping instructions do not establish an actual scoring-procedure change.

E4.justification: V2 extends existing analyses with early-training and layerwise diagnostics, PSNR-collapse traces for no normalization and eval-mode BatchNorm (Figure 4), and rescaling-related entropy comparisons (Figure 8). Network-size, bias-alignment, RPE and low-precision analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added entropy diagnostics concern feature distributions rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: The normalization-removal finding reverses substantially: v1 Table 5 reports usable results, including 26.86 dB on Urban100 versus LayerNorm's 26.55 dB; v2 Table 1 replaces these scores with dashes and Figures 4–5 report nonconvergence. Exact eval-mode BatchNorm scores are also removed, and new entropy findings appear. Main restoration, larger-model and quantization scores otherwise match.

T1.justification: The normalization definitions and rescaling mathematics are equivalent across versions. V2 simplifies notation and combines update equations; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The causal contribution is more cautiously framed: v1's abstract says it pinpoints the root cause, whereas v2 presents the normalization-bypass account as a perspective and hypothesis. Claims about the proposed components, restoration gains and reduced-precision robustness remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains larger super-resolution and deraining gains through reliable input information, and smaller denoising/JPEG gains through pervasive corruption (Section 4.2.2). It also expands the bias-compensation interpretation and revises the discussion of normalization removal around training failure.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies NVIDIA A6000 hardware but removes v1's Y-channel versus RGB scoring rules, border-cropping instructions and explicit additive-Gaussian-noise description. These are reproducibility-documentation changes; corresponding changes to actual procedures are not established.

R1.justification: V2 adds eight references, including the original BatchNorm, InstanceNorm and RMSNorm papers and additional restoration literature. These broaden attribution and context without substantially changing the work's positioning; the newly cited normalizers were already evaluated in v1.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around normalization, task and network-scale analyses, incorporating the former standalone benchmark discussion and reordering several analytical subsections.

P2.justification: V2 changes from two columns to one, consolidates benchmark tables into Table 2 and qualitative comparisons into Figure 6, redraws Figure 1, and combines depth, width and task plots. It also adds diagnostic figures and changes selected denoising/JPEG examples.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful convergence and entropy evidence and organizes the analysis more clearly. However, it replaces v1's successful normalization-free results with nonconvergence without explaining the discrepancy, while removing scoring details needed for reproduction. The PDFs do not establish whether the added explanatory support outweighs these unresolved reliability and reproducibility concerns.
